claude.market_view: The S&P 500 closed flat at 7,807 (-0.06%) and the Nasdaq fell 0.44% on Oct 12 as semis slid (SOX -2.7% intraday on China CXMT memory news), WTI rose ~2% to ~$93.7 and the dollar hit an 18-month high with the 10-year near 5.24%. Tuesday's open hinges on pre-market prints from JPM, GS, WFC, C, UNH, JNJ and DPZ, with a hot CPI (consensus 3.6% y/y) Wednesday capping risk appetite; banks enter down ~14% from their August peak, which sets a low bar.
lessons: TRAX gapped through my $37 target at the open, so the 'target hit' booked ~0%: once binary data is out before the open, the entry is already at the target. Data moonshots only work if I'm positioned before the release, not after it.

Weekend-news moonshots faded again: FRNM (-5.3%, stopped) and MIRM (-1.2%) both sold off from Sunday-release gaps, so I'm now 0-for-5 on buying overnight-news gaps and will only use scheduled, pre-open catalysts like earnings or confirmed event dates.

CBOE fell 3.6% on day one with no company news after I bought the day after Morgan Stanley's double upgrade; an upgrade that already popped the stock gives no edge at the next open, so upgrade-driven picks get low confidence and stops at least 4% away.

picks.thesis: UnitedHealth reports Q3 before the open Oct 13 (Investing.com preview, Oct 12: consensus EPS $4.12, revenue $111.31B, FY26 guide $19.50-20.00 vs $19.80 consensus, Q2 MCR 86.7% vs 88.1% FY guide). It closed $378.52, ~13% below its July level, and traded $381.92 after hours; options imply about ±7%. A contained MCR plus a reaffirmed or raised guide from the first managed-care reporter could squeeze a stock that has been flat for a month.
picks.main_risk: An MCR well above ~88% or an Optum Health miss would revive the utilization fears and the stock could gap down 7-10%; it is a coin-flip print, so liquidity is fine but direction isn't confirmed.

picks.thesis: Citigroup reports Q3 before the open Oct 13 (consensus EPS $2.65, revenue $23.72B per Investing.com, Oct 12). It closed $131.92 (+1.8%, 9.3M shares) on Oct 12, still ~11% below its $147.96 high, at ~11x forward earnings vs ~14x for JPM. With the bank index ~14% off its August peak, a clean credit print and strong markets/IB fees can drive a relief move.
picks.main_risk: Higher net credit losses or a weak NII outlook with the 10-year at 5.24% would extend the yield-driven bank selloff; Banamex deconsolidation charges could also muddy the headline.

It closed $264.03 (+1%, Benzinga) with defensives bid while semis sold off, ~6% below its $281 high. It has a record of beat-and-raise quarters, and a MedTech rebound after Q2's slowdown plus a guidance raise could lift it toward the high in one session.

claude.market_view: The S&P 500 finished flat at 7,805 and the Nasdaq slipped 0.15% on Oct 13 as semis/memory sold off for a 6th session on China CXMT news and AMAT fell 6.7% after its investor day, while bank prints (JPM miss, GS beat) faded intraday. Wednesday hinges on September CPI at 8:30am (consensus headline +0.6% m/m, core +0.2%) plus pre-market prints from ASML, MS, BAC (new $1.2B AML/sanctions charge) and BLK; my moonshots are a concentrated bet that ASML's 1am report relieves the oversold chip-equipment group, so they are highly correlated with each other.
lessons: Pre-open earnings moonshots were bought after the news: DPZ and JNJ opened below my stops (set off the prior close) and were out at the open even though DPZ later traded to $305, so moonshot stops must sit below the plausible post-print open, not just below yesterday's close.

Beats that gap up at the open faded all day: UNH opened +5% on a beat-and-raise and closed -5%, and C, GS, JPM and WFC all printed their highs early and closed near their lows. Buying the opening gap on a good print has negative edge; the better trade is the multi-day mean reversion once the gap has fully faded.
Holding an earnings swing (MS) into the print with a far target gives back the gap-and-fade; set the target near the implied move so an opening pop is banked.

The ADR has fallen from $1,834 (Oct 6) to $1,717.76 (Oct 13 close, ~1.4M average volume), so a solid guide can unwind the CXMT/AMAT-driven selloff; options imply about ±5.6%.

last_review.reason: Rose 1.75% Tuesday after the BofA double upgrade ($285 target) as follow-through builds; above entry.

open.thesis: T-Mobile fell ~12% Friday on SpaceX's 800 MHz spectrum deal. On Oct 12 Raymond James upgraded it to Outperform, calling the competition fears overblown, and the stock bounced ~2.9% to ~$152 on 9M shares vs 4.9M average (Benzinga), near its $147.90 52-week low at ~10.5x forward P/E with $16B FCF. last_review.reason: The oversold rebound continues (+1.2% Tuesday to $153.73) after the Raymond James upgrade; above entry.
